order.why_here: The base case: read a number as columns, and delete the lowest 1 with n & (n - 1) so work scales with the answer.
Counts for 0..n reuse each other: popcount(i) = popcount(i >> 1) + (i & 1), a DP over shifts.
Moves bits between columns with shifts and shows why a fixed 32-bit width must be imposed in Python.
Introduces XOR as pair cancellation and column parity: equal values vanish.
Reuses Single Number's trick by manufacturing the pairs yourself: indices against values.
The low two bits decide a greedy move; a +1 carry clears a run of 1s in one step.
Words become 26-bit sets; submask enumeration from the small (puzzle) side flips the loop.
XOR as ten parity counters plus prefix masks and first-seen positions, with 11 partner masks per step.
Closes the chapter: binary trie with top-down greedy for max XOR, plus offline sorting so the trie only grows.
